observations.notes: Claim boundary present: a London non-profit, data access via subject access requests, investigations challenging unfair management and automated dismissals, collective action against Uber's dynamic pay; data trusts are omitted. 'Coordinates group lawsuits' compresses the record (Stichting WIE International launched the collective action; WIE's investigations support strategic litigation); 'operating also as Stichting WIE International' merges the two names, which the census registers as aliases. Framework read as workers' digital rights under the law: 'digital and labor rights' and SARs carry it. Purpose present: transparency over pay, allocation and performance, and challenging unfair algorithmic management (the record's 'turn data into power ... holding tech platforms to account'). Commitments absent: acting on behalf of workers in support of unions and grassroots organisations through data trusts is not carried; the 'Research & Alliances' bullet (University of Oxford, the TUC) is not in the saved sources (a card dated Apr 29, 2026 carries the TUC report) and is not judged. Deposit chain absent: 'landmark research' names no report. Founder, date, lineage and identifier are unknown in the records and not scored.
